base_member_text: Cross-line: in OneWayCoupling every boundary separator line ('! east' etc.) is list-directed READ into TIME_COUPLING_2 (L376, L395, L401, L422, L428, L449, L455, L476) - the commented-out originals (L375 etc.) read the line without a variable; if the separator line is non-numeric text the read yields IOstatus>0 (error, not EOF) which is not trapped by 'IF (IOstatus < 0)', leaving TIME_COUPLING_2 undefined by that statement; the real next time was already read at L371, so these reads at best re-consume separator lines and at worst overwrite the time level
audit_member_text: The initial reader consumes each side label/separator with a list-directed READ having no item (east L102; analogous west/south/north L121, L138, L155). The update routine's replacements instead read every separator into TIME_COUPLING_2 (east L376, west L401, south L428, north L455, plus absent-side branches L395, L422, L449, L476). This overwrites the actual time read at L371 with non-time side records or advances the numeric time incorrectly, a repeated copy/port mismatch that corrupts schedule parsing.

base_member_text: EOF handling: GOTO 120 from any partial read (L372-477) jumps past all remaining boundary reads to L483, so a truncated last record leaves slot-2 arrays partially updated while TIME_COUPLING_1 was already advanced (L368)

PARALLEL overlap test @L182-183 (and east/south/north analogues) combines '>Nghost .AND. <Nloc-Nghost+1' terms with .OR. in a way that treats one-endpoint-inside as partial overlap; the full-span case is handled separately @L195-199 - boundary-case correctness at exact subdomain edges depends on these inequalities being exclusive

Ghost-cell fill loops use fixed local ghost ranges I=1..Nghost (west L508) and I=Iend+1..Iend+Nghost (east L532) etc., while coupling array index J-Nghost+Kshift_* must stay within 1..N_COUPLING_*; no explicit bounds check on the index expression
Format 119 (5E16.6) requires the nesting file rows to wrap every 5 values; declared twice (L114, L363) with the same label in different scopes
OneWayCoupling interpolates and overwrites ETA/U/V/HU/HV only in ghost cells - interior is untouched (one-way nesting); no ETA0/masking interaction in this file

audit_member_text: Both the initial equal-time state and EOF collapse interpolation weights to zero: TIME_COUPLING_2 is initialized equal to TIME_COUPLING_1 (L93-L95), while equal slots set tmp1=tmp2=ZERO (L488-L497). At EOF, TIME_COUPLING_1 is first advanced to TIME_COUPLING_2, the failed read jumps to L483 (L367-L372), and the same equal-slot branch zeros every coupled ETA/U/V ghost value at L509-L588 instead of retaining the last boundary record.
dispositions.rationale: span-verified 2026-08-28 by Codex deep re-audit: Both initialization and EOF leave equal time slots, and the equal-slot branch sets both weights to zero rather than retaining either record. Those weights directly zero coupled ETA/U/V ghosts, with no later boundary restoration before they are used.
